meta.notes: 16 watersheds covered, 17 still need research. 7 city programs (Minneapolis, St. Louis Park, Eden Prairie, Roseville, Burnsville, Apple Valley, Lakeville). 8 county programs (Dakota, Carver, Scott, Ramsey, Washington, Anoka, Hennepin Good Steward + Opportunity Grants).

maintenance.process: Check each URL, verify amounts/eligibility still current, update JSON

field_reference.name: Display name of the program
field_reference.property_types: Array: residential, commercial, church, school, nonprofit, hoa, municipal, institutional
field_reference.match_required: Cost share percentage required from applicant (e.g. '50%', '25-50%')
field_reference.url: Link to program info or application
field_reference.link_text: OPTIONAL - Custom button text. Default is 'Learn more & apply →'. Use 'Learn more →' for info-only pages, 'Contact district →' for programs requiring direct contact.
field_reference.needs_research: Set to true if details are unverified/incomplete
field_reference.restrict_to_counties: OPTIONAL - Array of county names (lowercase) to limit statewide programs to specific counties

statewide_programs.name: Lawns to Legumes
statewide_programs.eligibility_note: Must have outdoor planting space. Renters welcome.
statewide_programs.notes: Weighted lottery with priority for habitat areas and environmental justice factors. Currently closed — next application window expected Spring 2027.

statewide_programs.name: Hennepin County Opportunity Grants
statewide_programs.eligibility_note: For larger projects leveraging multiple funding sources. Hennepin County properties only. Pre-application meeting recommended.
statewide_programs.application_timeline: Currently closed — check back for future rounds
statewide_programs.notes: Great for institutions, nonprofits, churches planning significant native restoration. Can be used as match for other funding sources.

programs.name: Clean Water Project Grant
programs.match_required: As low as 0-5% for residents (25% for businesses). Some locations qualify for reduced rates.
programs.eligibility_note: Must be within Capitol Region Watershed District boundaries. Site visit included before project approval.
programs.notes: One of the most generous programs in the metro — 95-100% reimbursement for residents. Some locations may qualify for full coverage. 10-year maintenance commitment required.

programs.name: Clean Water Project Maintenance Grant
programs.eligibility_note: For non-residential properties with previous CRWD-funded projects. Covers weeding, plant replacement, erosion repair, mulching, etc.
programs.notes: Helps businesses, churches, HOAs, schools maintain existing installations. Volunteer hours count toward match.

programs.name: Residential Cost Share (via city/county partners)
programs.eligibility_note: MCWD does not offer direct residential grants. Homeowners should contact their city or county for local cost-share options.
programs.notes: Contact your city for available programs.

programs.name: Land & Water Partnership Program
programs.eligibility_note: For municipalities and large-scale private developers/landowners with capacity to lead project implementation.
programs.notes: Technical and financial support from concept through construction. High-impact regional projects.

programs.name: Landscape Level 1 Grant
programs.amount: Up to $5,000 ($7,500 for curb cut rain gardens)
programs.notes: 25-50% reimbursement (75% for curb cuts). First come, first served.

programs.name: Soil Health Grant
programs.notes: 75% reimbursement. Good entry point for smaller projects.

programs.name: Stewardship Grants (Residential)
programs.notes: 50-100% funding depending on project type and location. Site consultation required before applying.

programs.name: Stewardship Grants (Commercial/Institutional)
programs.notes: 50-100% funding depending on project type and location. Requests over $5k need Board approval. Great option for churches, schools, HOAs.

programs.name: Maintenance Funding
programs.eligibility_note: For properties with RWMWD grant-funded projects completed within last 5 years.
programs.notes: Covers weeding, plant replacement, and erosion repair on existing grant-funded projects.

programs.name: Mini-Grants Program
programs.notes: One application per year. First come, first served. Reimbursement-based.

programs.name: Water Quality Grants
programs.notes: 25-50% funding typical, up to 75% for highly beneficial projects.

programs.name: Partnership Cost Share Program
project_types: conversion of impervious surfaces to native plants
programs.eligibility_note: $10,000 minimum — best suited for larger residential or commercial projects. Contact your city to apply.
programs.notes: Reimbursement-based. For smaller projects, check other programs listed for your area.

programs.name: Partnership Cost Share Program
project_types: conversion of impervious surfaces to native plants
programs.eligibility_note: $10,000 minimum — best suited for larger residential or commercial projects. Contact your city to apply.
programs.notes: Reimbursement-based. For smaller projects, check other programs listed for your area.

programs.name: Cost Share Grant Program
programs.amount: Up to $6,250 residential (more for HOAs, commercial, nonprofits)
programs.notes: Two funding tiers — habitat/native plantings and stormwater projects. Priority funding for equity zones.

programs.name: Community Grants
programs.eligibility_note: NOT for individuals or private businesses. Nonprofits, schools, neighborhood groups, HOAs, and government only. Individuals can partner with an eligible org to apply.
programs.notes: No match required. Two rounds annually. About 3 months from application to funding. Must complete within 1 year.

programs.name: Planning Grants
programs.eligibility_note: NOT for individuals or private businesses. For developing water quality or habitat initiative plans.
programs.notes: Use this to develop a plan, then apply for a separate MWMO grant to build it. Two rounds annually. Must complete within 1 year.

programs.name: Action Grants
programs.eligibility_note: NOT for individuals or private businesses. For projects ready for immediate implementation.
programs.notes: Two rounds annually. Competitive — not all projects funded. Prioritizes underserved populations and environmentally sensitive areas. Must complete within 1 year.

programs.name: No Direct Watershed Program
programs.eligibility_note: BCWMC does not offer direct grants. Check your city for local programs.
programs.notes: Watershed provides education and resources but funding comes through member cities or statewide programs like Lawns to Legumes.

programs.name: Landscaping for Clean Water Grant
programs.eligibility_note: Must complete free Landscaping for Clean Water class first (registration closes June 18, 2026). Available to Dakota County residents and west-side St. Paul residents within the Lower Mississippi River Watershed.
programs.notes: Grant upon project completion. Class + design course required. On-site technical assistance included. 3 application rounds in 2026.

programs.name: Cost Share via Washington Conservation District
programs.eligibility_note: VBWD partners with Washington Conservation District for cost share programs. Contact WCD directly for current program details and to request a site visit.
programs.notes: WCD staff can help with design and connect you to available funding.

programs.name: Cost Share via Washington Conservation District
programs.eligibility_note: Middle St. Croix WMO partners with Washington Conservation District for cost share programs. Contact WCD directly for current program details and to request a site visit.
programs.notes: WCD staff can help with design and connect you to available funding.

programs.name: Nine Mile Creek Cost Share Program
programs.amount: Up to $6,250 residential (more for HOAs, commercial, nonprofits)
programs.eligibility_note: Richfield and Bloomington residents are served by Nine Mile Creek Watershed District.
programs.notes: Two funding tiers — habitat/native plantings and stormwater projects. Richfield is a priority equity zone with reserved funding.

programs.name: Water Quality Cost Share Program
programs.notes: Free site visit and concept design included. Small grants track available (up to $500) for smaller residential projects.

programs.name: Cost Share Incentive Program
programs.eligibility_note: Must apply before starting your project.
programs.application_timeline: Applications typically open at beginning of each year — check website for current cycle status
programs.notes: Reimbursement-based. $500 minimum award. Contact the district for current availability.

programs.name: Landscaping for Clean Water Grant
programs.eligibility_note: Must complete Landscaping for Clean Water workshop first. WMO budgets for ~12 projects/year. Registration closes June 18, 2026.
programs.notes: Workshops and design assistance provided by Dakota County SWCD.

programs.name: Residential Stormwater Credit
programs.amount: 35% stormwater bill reduction (45% in Green Zones)
programs.eligibility_note: Ongoing annual savings — not a one-time grant. Rain barrels alone don't qualify. Practices must be on your property and treat runoff from your impervious surfaces.
programs.notes: One of the most valuable incentives in Minneapolis — saves money every year, not just once.

programs.name: Rainwater Rewards Program
programs.application_timeline: Year-round until funds are exhausted. Must be approved before starting work.
programs.eligibility_note: Two tracks: Rain garden lottery (city manages design and construction) or DIY reimbursement. One project per fiscal year.
programs.notes: Rain garden lottery is a great low-cost option — the city handles design and construction. Maintenance agreement required.

programs.name: Landscaping for Water Quality Rebate
project_types: invasive species removal (as part of larger water quality project)
programs.eligibility_note: Requires city permit approval before starting work. At least 75% native species required. 5-year maintenance commitment. Site visit recommended before applying.
programs.application_timeline: Year-round, first-come first-served until funds exhausted. Project must be completed within one year of approval.
programs.notes: Reimbursement-based — city inspects before and after. May be stackable with watershed district grants (Nine Mile Creek, RPBCWD).

programs.name: Stormwater Utility Fee Credit
programs.eligibility_note: Ongoing annual savings — not a one-time grant. Practices must comply with city standards and be approved by Engineering. Renewal required every 5 years.
programs.notes: Larger credits for practices that handle more runoff. Periodic inspections required.

programs.name: Neighborhood Water Resources Enhancement Grant
programs.eligibility_note: Reimbursement-based — only make purchases after grant agreement is signed. Priority given to applicants who completed Dakota County SWCD's Landscaping for Clean Water workshop.
programs.notes: Reimbursement-based. Must include plant selections, site dimensions, and maintenance plans. Can stack with Dakota County SWCD grants.

programs.name: Rainwater Rewards Grant Program
programs.eligibility_note: Native plants encouraged for water quality and pollinator habitat. Projects cannot be in easements without city permission. First-come, first-served.
programs.notes: Reimbursement-based — receipts and photos required. Rain gardens and shoreline projects given priority.

programs.name: Landscaping for Clean Water Rebate
programs.eligibility_note: Must complete Landscaping for Clean Water workshop in the current year. Limited to first 10 applicants. One rebate per address.
programs.application_timeline: After completing LCW workshop — limited spots
programs.notes: Stacks with Dakota County SWCD grant ($250+) for a potential combined $500+. Modest but easy to access.

programs.name: Landscaping for Clean Water
programs.eligibility_note: Must complete free Landscaping for Clean Water class and design course first. Registration closes June 18, 2026.
programs.notes: On-site technical assistance included. Class + design course required. Can combine with watershed grants for more total funding.

programs.name: Improving Water Quality Cost Share
programs.notes: Very generous cost share — among the best in the metro.

programs.name: Pollinator Habitat Program
programs.eligibility_note: Minimum project size: 250 square feet.
programs.notes: Convert turf or non-native landscapes to pollinator habitat.

programs.name: Natural Landscaping Program
programs.notes: Contact Scott SWCD for current program details and application process.

programs.name: Conservation District Cost-Share
programs.notes: Works through local watershed partners. Contact the district for current funding availability.

programs.name: Conservation District Financial Assistance
programs.amount: Varies — partners with all 8 watershed orgs in the county
programs.notes: WCD connects residents to available funding across watershed districts. Good umbrella resource for Washington County.

programs.name: Cost Share Grant Program
programs.amount: Up to 75% of project costs (95% for street runoff practices)
programs.eligibility_note: Projects that capture street or parking lot runoff may qualify for 95% funding. Discuss your project with ACD staff before applying.
programs.notes: Very generous for curb-cut rain gardens (up to 95%). Grant amount based on natural resource benefits and cost effectiveness.

programs.name: Good Steward Grants
programs.application_timeline: Check Hennepin County website for current round
programs.notes: All landowners eligible including individual homeowners. Smaller and more accessible than Opportunity Grants. In-kind contributions can count toward 25% match. Great for larger residential prairie restorations.
